newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: PRESS DIGEST - Sri Lanka Newspapers - October 2.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Sri Lanka Newspapers - October 2.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the Sri Lankan press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
President Chandrika Kumaratunga appeals for donors of blood to save lives of soldiers wounded in latest fighting against Tamil Tiger rebels.
Opposition leader Ranil Wickremasinghe says United National Party will announce stand on third party mediation to solve ethnic conflict only after government does so.
United Nations assures Sri Lanka of help to rebuild war-torn north.
National hospital postpones non-urgent surgery after stocks at blood bank run down following heavy demand from army hospital to treat soldiers wounded in latest offensive against Tamil rebels.
President Kumaratunga urges top priority for new highways projects.

Police arrest Tamil teacher in Nuwara Eliya on suspicion of involvement in LTTE plan to kill President Kumaratunga. He had taken pictures of route used by Kumaratunga and landing pad for her helicopter.
LTTE loses key source of funds after fall of their northern Kilinochchi stronghold.
Tamil Tiger rebels plundered stocks of medicine before their Kilinochchi stronghold fell to advancing army.
